messages.content:
You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE battle (
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    date TEXT,
    bulgarian_commander TEXT,
    latin_commander TEXT,
    result TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE ship (
    lost_in_battle INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    tonnage TEXT,
    ship_type TEXT,
    location TEXT,
    disposition_of_ship TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (lost_in_battle) REFERENCES battle(id)
);

CREATE TABLE death (
    caused_by_ship_id INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    note TEXT,
    killed INT,
    injured INT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (caused_by_ship_id) REFERENCES ship(id)
);

Do you want a list of all battles in the `battle` table, or only battles matching some criteria (date range, result, commander, etc.)?

If you just want all recorded battles:

```sql
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  date,
  bulgarian_commander,
  latin_commander,
  result
FROM battle
ORDER BY date, name;
```

If you tell me what “historical battles” should mean here (e.g., all battles with known date, or only wins/losses, or involving a specific side/commander), I can tailor the query.
focus on battles where more than 10 people died

```sql
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  b.bulgarian_commander,
  b.latin_commander,
  b.result,
  SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) AS total_killed
FROM battle b
JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY
  b.id, b.name, b.date, b.bulgarian_commander, b.latin_commander, b.result
HAVING SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) > 10
ORDER BY total_killed DESC, b.date, b.name;
```
total deaths should be more than 10 for all sides combined.

```sql
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  b.bulgarian_commander,
  b.latin_commander,
  b.result,
  SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) AS total_deaths_all_sides
FROM battle b
JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY
  b.id, b.name, b.date, b.bulgarian_commander, b.latin_commander, b.result
HAVING SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) > 10
ORDER BY total_deaths_all_sides DESC, b.date, b.name;
```

This sums `death.killed` across every ship associated with the battle (i.e., all sides combined), then filters to totals > 10.
also include battle names with IDs

```sql
SELECT
  b.id AS battle_id,
  b.name AS battle_name,
  b.date,
  b.bulgarian_commander,
  b.latin_commander,
  b.result,
  SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) AS total_deaths_all_sides
FROM battle b
JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY
  b.id, b.name, b.date, b.bulgarian_commander, b.latin_commander, b.result
HAVING SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) > 10
ORDER BY total_deaths_all_sides DESC, b.date, b.name;
```
also need unique identifiers for the battles

`battle.id` is already the unique identifier (it’s the PRIMARY KEY). If you want it explicitly returned as the unique battle identifier along with the name:

```sql
SELECT
  b.id AS battle_uid,
  b.name AS battle_name,
  b.date,
  b.bulgarian_commander,
  b.latin_commander,
  b.result,
  SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) AS total_deaths_all_sides
FROM battle b
JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY
  b.id, b.name, b.date, b.bulgarian_commander, b.latin_commander, b.result
HAVING SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) > 10
ORDER BY total_deaths_all_sides DESC, b.date, b.name;
```

If you meant a different kind of identifier (e.g., a generated UUID/string), tell me the format you need.
